analysis_summary: Suspicious activity detected involving mshta.exe executing a script from a GitHub URL, potentially downloading malicious payloads and modifying system settings. The process also made outbound network connections and accessed sensitive registry keys. The event log clearing (EventID 1102) suggests an attempt to cover tracks.
reasoning: The investigation identified the execution of `mshta.exe` via `cmd.exe` with a command line referencing a script hosted on GitHub (`https://raw.githubusercontent.com/redcanaryco/atomic-red-team/master/atomics/T1218.005/src/mshta.sct`). This is a common technique for malware delivery and execution (T1218.005). The `mshta.exe` process subsequently loaded DLLs associated with internet access (`urlmon.dll`, `winhttp.dll`) and performed suspicious registry modifications, including accessing sensitive keys like `\\REGISTRY\\MACHINE\\SYSTEM\\ControlSet001\\Control\\Lsa` and `ZoneMap`. These actions, combined with outbound network connections initiated by `mshta.exe` (to 151.101.248.133 on port 443), indicate a high likelihood of malicious activity. Additionally, the `svchost.exe` process was observed calling privileged services with `SeTcbPrivilege`, which could indicate an attempt at privilege escalation. The clearing of the audit log (EventID 1102) by the user 'wardog' further supports the suspicious nature of these events, indicating an attempt to hide malicious actions.
